description: Inferno SMART App Launch test kit v1.0.3, SMART App Launch STU2.2 Client suite, all four client types. Inferno plays the EHR and authorization server; `swiss` names a finding Swiss must have shown.

public/smart_client_registration_alp_ver.reason: The harness serves Swiss over http://localhost, and the suite requires https for registered launch and redirect URIs (SMART App Launch 2.2). A Swiss deployed over HTTPS passes this; it is about the harness, not Swiss.

public/smart_client_access_alp_interacti.reason: Swiss signs in standalone and by EHR launch, then reads Patient/85 with the token. Swiss also reports, on every sign-in, that the ID token from Inferno's simulated server omits the nonce Swiss sent, which OpenID Connect requires it to echo: a finding about that server, kept here so a change in it shows up.

public/smart_client_authorization_reques.reason: Swiss's authorize requests: PKCE S256, state, aud, launch on the EHR launch and launch/patient on the standalone one.

public/smart_client_token_request_alp_ve.reason: A public client's code exchange: client_id and code_verifier, no secret.

public/smart_client_token_use_verificati.reason: The FHIR read carries the access token Inferno issued.

symmetric/smart_client_registration_alcs.reason: The harness serves Swiss over http://localhost, and the suite requires https for registered launch and redirect URIs (SMART App Launch 2.2). A Swiss deployed over HTTPS passes this; it is about the harness, not Swiss.

symmetric/smart_client_access_alcs_inter.reason: As for the public client, with client_secret_basic. Swiss also reports, on every sign-in, that the ID token from Inferno's simulated server omits the nonce Swiss sent, which OpenID Connect requires it to echo: a finding about that server, kept here so a change in it shows up.

symmetric/smart_client_token_request_alc.reason: The code exchange authenticates with client_secret_basic.

symmetric/smart_client_token_use_verific.reason: The FHIR read carries the access token Inferno issued.

asymmetric/smart_client_registration_alc.reason: The harness serves Swiss over http://localhost, and the suite requires https for registered launch and redirect URIs (SMART App Launch 2.2). A Swiss deployed over HTTPS passes this; it is about the harness, not Swiss. It also warns that the JWKS is given inline rather than by URL, which is how the harness registers it.

asymmetric/smart_client_access_alca_inte.reason: As for the public client, with a private_key_jwt client assertion signed by the key imported in the environments file. Swiss also reports, on every sign-in, that the ID token from Inferno's simulated server omits the nonce Swiss sent, which OpenID Connect requires it to echo: a finding about that server, kept here so a change in it shows up.

asymmetric/smart_client_token_request_al.reason: The code exchange authenticates with a private_key_jwt assertion (new in 3.2) that Inferno verifies against the registered JWKS.

asymmetric/smart_client_token_use_verifi.reason: The FHIR read carries the access token Inferno issued.

backend/smart_client_registration_bsca_v.reason: A Backend Services client registers only its id and JWKS.

backend/smart_client_access_bsca_interac.reason: Swiss gets a client_credentials token with a signed assertion and reads Patient/85 with it.

backend/smart_client_token_request_bsca_.reason: The client_credentials request carries a signed assertion Inferno verifies against the registered JWKS.

backend/smart_client_token_use_verificat.reason: The FHIR read carries the access token Inferno issued.
